verdicts.justification:
Repro output matched the claim exactly: '0 37
5 42
10 47
11 0
12 1'. With duration=4, tail_duration=1, frame_rate=12 the faint trail holds 37-47 of 48 interpolated points during frames 0-10 (i.e. nearly the whole FUTURE trajectory rendered as a 'past' trail), then drops to 0 at frame 11 and restarts at 1. Evidence PNG ctshort_frame010.png shows the full spiral faint with only a short opaque head; ctshort_frame011.png shows the trail vanished. Classic negative-slice (data[max(0, i-w):i] missing) bug; clearly-wrong visual on a documented feature.

Repro printed 'gif frames: 1' for animate=True + continuous hue in 2-D (all frames pixel-identical, Pillow merges). My no-hue control with identical parameters printed 'no-hue gif frames: 24', proving the hue path is what kills the animation. Evidence s7_chue_precog_f04.png shows the full multicolored trajectory fully opaque at frame 4 (no reveal, no precog dimming) while s7_nohue_precog_f04.png shows the correct opaque-head + faint-future rendering. Animate + per-observation hue silently renders static content on matplotlib.

Repro output matched exactly: 'crash: `x` must contain at least 2 elements.' for [trajectory, single-point] order, and 'frames when single point first: 1' for the reversed order (silent 1-frame animation of a 40-point trajectory). Plotting a reference point alongside a trajectory is reasonable use; one order crashes with a raw scipy message, the other silently degrades.

Repro printed 'frame-0 azim: 0.0' for animate='spin', azim=45. My control with animate='serial', azim=45 printed 'serial frame-0 azim: 45.0', confirming the claimed inconsistency between animation styles.

verdicts.justification: Repro printed 'Figure []' -- animate=2 yields a static Figure with zero warnings. Control: animate='bogus' raises "ValueError: unknown animate style 'bogus'; valid styles are 'parallel', 'spin', 'serial', 'morph', 'window' (or True/False)...", so string validation exists but non-bool/non-string truthy values silently fall through to static.

verdicts.justification: Repro raised exactly 'ValueError: The truth value of an array with more than one element is ambiguous. Use a.any() or a.all()' for chemtrails=np.array([True, False]), while chemtrails=[True, False] is the documented per-dataset form. Secondary claim also verified: chemtrails='yes' silently coerced to True ('str flag trail artists: 1').

Behavior reproduces: animate='chemtrails' with explicit chemtrails=False renders 'trail artists: 1' with 'warnings: []' -- silent override, no warning. HOWEVER the claimed precedent is overstated: the dict form does NOT raise on this same conflict. I tested animate={'style': 'parallel', 'chemtrails': True}, chemtrails=False -> 'no error'. plot.py:1284 only raises when the flat value differs from the LITERAL default, and chemtrails=False IS the default, so an explicit False is fundamentally indistinguishable from 'not passed' in both forms. Downgraded major->n/a, minor->style: a warning would require a sentinel-default refactor, and the sugar honoring its own name is defensible.

Repro output matched exactly: 'head last: [0.4991, -0.8696, -0.0738]' vs 'trail first: [0.7064, -0.709, -0.0529]' -- the opaque head and faint future trail do not share a vertex, leaving a one-interpolation-step gap in the rendered line.

Repro printed 'head pts: 0' -- tail_duration=-1 is accepted without any validation and yields an animation whose opaque head is empty at frame 12 (mid-animation), i.e. silent garbage output for invalid input.

Repro printed 'frames: 40 expected: 24' -- marker-only (fmt='.') parallel animation uses raw row count as frame count. The docstring documents 'duration (animation only) : float / Length of the animation in seconds (default: 30 seconds)' (plot.py:791-792), so 40 frames at frame_rate=12 (3.33 s instead of 2 s) breaks the documented contract.

Both animated and static plots raised exactly 'ValueError: `y` must contain only finite values.' Nuance the auditor did not mention: before the crash, hypertools DOES emit 'UserWarning: PPCA cannot fill 3 row(s) with no observed features at all; those rows will remain NaN. Use model=Kalman...', so the user gets a hint -- but the terminal error is still a raw scipy message with no hypertools-level guidance, so the claim stands as filed (minor).

verdicts.justification: Repro raised 'CalledProcessError: Command [ffmpeg, -f, rawvideo, ... -vcodec, h264, ...] returned non-zero exit status 1' after ffmpeg printed 'Error initializing the muxer for .../anim.xyz: Invalid argument'. Unrecognized extensions fall through to the ffmpeg writer and leak a raw subprocess error instead of naming supported formats.
